opportunities.name: GitHub candidate lead research and email
opportunities.description: Look up a GitHub user, note their follower count, top repo (stars, language) and latest post, then draft a lead email to hiring for a given role.
steps: Open GitHub and click 'Search or jump to'
Type the GitHub username and press Enter
Click the 'Users' results filter
Open the matching user profile
Open their top pinned/popular repo and note stars and language; note follower count and latest blog post
Open mail compose
Set To = hiring address
Set Subject = 'Lead for {role}: {username}'
Set Body = '{username}: {followers} followers, top repo {repo} ({stars} stars, {language}), latest post: {post}.'
Send/save the draft

instances.values: username=simonw, repo=llm (no email seen; possibly unfinished)

opportunities.name: Nearest amenity walking distance + neighborhood summary note
opportunities.description: Find the nearest amenity of a given type to an address on OpenStreetMap, get walking distance/time, look up the neighborhood on Wikipedia, and record a note.
steps: On OpenStreetMap, search '{amenity} near {address}'
Open the closest result
Click 'Find directions between two points' and choose Foot
Set From = address, To = the chosen place, press Enter; note distance and time
On Wikipedia, search the neighborhood and read the summary
In Notes, add a note: '{address}: nearest {amenity} {place}, {distance}, {time} walk. {neighborhood}: {summary}'

instances.values: address=350 5th Ave, New York; amenity=library; neighborhood=Midtown Manhattan
coffee near Union Square (Wikipedia step started; no note seen)
OSM search, then Wikipedia 'Chicago Loop' (no note seen)

opportunities.name: Executive bio + archived company homepage note
opportunities.description: Look up a person on Wikipedia and their company's homepage in a given year on the Wayback Machine, then record a note.
steps: Search Wikipedia for the person and note their birth date and role
On the Wayback Machine, enter the company domain and press Enter
Choose the target year and a capture date
Note the homepage's main headline
In Notes, add: '{person}: born {date}, {role}. {domain} in {year}: {headline}'
